skill.title: React
skill.summary: State as a snapshot, component identity, effects and data-fetching correctness.
skill.description: Reason about rendering precisely: how state updates are applied, how keys preserve identity, when effects run, and how to avoid stale or out-of-order data.

questions.title: Three updates, one click
questions.prompt: `count` starts at 0. After one click, what is rendered?
questions.hint: What is the value of `count` inside this particular render's event handler?

options.text: 0, until the component re-renders a second time
It varies between renders because updates race

questions.explanation: State is a snapshot for each render. All three calls compute `0 + 1` and queue the value 1. To apply successive updates, pass an updater function: `setCount(c => c + 1)`.
rubric: Explains that `count` is fixed within a render (state as a snapshot).
Recognises all three calls queue the same value.
Proposes the updater function form for sequential updates.
misconceptions: Batched updates are applied in a nondeterministic order.

resources.title: React: Queueing a series of state updates

questions.acceptance_criteria: Answers 1 and explains that state is a per-render snapshot.

questions.title: Index keys in a reorderable list
questions.prompt: Each row in a to-do list contains an uncontrolled `<input>`. The list uses `key={index}`, and new items are inserted at the top. What goes wrong?

options.text: React logs a duplicate-key warning on every insert
Typed input text stays at the old positions and appears next to the wrong items
The list re-renders more slowly, but behaves correctly
Nothing; keys only need to be unique among siblings

questions.explanation: React uses keys to match elements between renders. With index keys, inserting at the top shifts every index, so React reuses each existing component (and its DOM and state) for a different item. Use a stable id from the data as the key.
rubric: Explains that keys determine component identity across renders.
Describes state or DOM attaching to the wrong item after insertion.
Recommends stable ids derived from the data.
misconceptions: Index keys are only a performance concern.
Any key that is unique among siblings is sufficient, even if it changes.
questions.acceptance_criteria: Explains that index keys attach state to the wrong items after insertion and recommends stable ids.

questions.title: An effect that runs too often
questions.prompt: The network tab shows this effect fetching on every render, even when `userId` hasn't changed. Why?

options.text: `useEffect` always runs on every render in development
`options` is a new object each render, so the dependency compares unequal
`fetchProfile` must be listed as a dependency
Effects that call `setState` always re-trigger themselves

questions.explanation: React compares dependencies with `Object.is`. A new object literal is created on every render, so the dependency always changes. Depend on the primitive (`userId`) and build the object inside the effect, or memoise it if it must be shared.
rubric: Identifies that dependencies are compared by identity (`Object.is`).
Explains that the object literal is recreated each render.
Fixes it by depending on primitives or moving the object inside the effect.
misconceptions: Development-mode double invocation explains repeated effects on every render.
questions.acceptance_criteria: Identifies the new object identity on each render as the cause and fixes the dependency.

questions.title: State that should be derived
questions.prompt: Review this component. What problems does the `fullName` state cause, and how would you rewrite it?
questions.hint: Can `fullName` ever hold information that isn't already in `first` and `last`?
questions.explanation: `fullName` is redundant: it is fully determined by `first` and `last`. Syncing it in an effect causes an extra render with stale data first, adds a place for the copies to disagree, and is more code. Compute it during render; reach for `useMemo` only when the calculation is genuinely expensive.
rubric: Identifies `fullName` as derived from existing state.
Explains the extra render and the brief stale value caused by syncing in an effect.
Rewrites it as a value computed during render.
Mentions `useMemo` only for expensive derivations, not as the default.
misconceptions: Every value shown in the UI must live in state.
Effects are the right tool for keeping two pieces of state in sync.

resources.title: React: You might not need an effect

questions.acceptance_criteria: Identifies fullName as derived state and computes it during render instead of syncing it in an effect.

questions.title: Out-of-order responses
questions.prompt: A user clicks quickly between profiles A and B. The request for A is slow, so it resolves after B and the page ends up showing A while B is selected. Explain why this happens and implement a fix. Mention what a data-fetching library would handle for you.
questions.hint: What runs when `userId` changes before the earlier request finishes?
questions.explanation: Each `userId` change starts a new request, but nothing stops an earlier one from resolving later and overwriting newer state. Use the effect cleanup to ignore stale results (a boolean flag) or cancel them with `AbortController`. Libraries such as TanStack Query or SWR key requests by their inputs and handle this, plus caching and retries.
rubric: Explains that responses can resolve in a different order from requests.
Uses the effect cleanup to ignore or abort stale requests.
Shows correct cleanup code (an ignore flag or `AbortController`).
Mentions handling errors and loading state, not only the happy path.
Notes that data-fetching libraries key requests by input and handle this case.
misconceptions: Requests always resolve in the order they were sent.
Effect cleanup only matters when the component unmounts.
questions.acceptance_criteria: Explains out-of-order resolution and fixes it with effect cleanup (an ignore flag or AbortController).
